--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.node_redundancy()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Compute the redundancy coefficient of nodes in a bipartite graph. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.node_redundancy()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | EdgeCase description: Compute the redundancy coefficient of nodes in a bipartite graph. title: >- [Graph.node_redundancy()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Compute the redundancy coefficient of nodes in a bipartite graph. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Compute the redundancy coefficient of nodes in a bipartite graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L24575-L24697){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.node_redundancy(nodes=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Node redundancy](../assets/graphs/node-redundancy.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same people and events graph. ann attended party and talk, and bob attended both too, so the pair stays linked without ann: ann scores 1.0, and bob, covered by ann, also 1.0. cy is the only one at both talk and game, so the edges joining them, in the accent color, are the pair's sole link and cy scores 0.0." width="100%"} The redundancy of a node (Latapy et al., 2008) is the fraction of pairs of its neighbors that are also linked through some other node: if a person attends two events, would the two events still share an attendee without that person? A redundancy of 1 means the node's co-memberships are all duplicated by others, so removing it would not change the projection onto the other side; a redundancy of 0 means the node is the only link between each pair of its groups (a broker). Every node reported must have at least two neighbors. Edge direction and parallel edges are ignored. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional nodes (IDs or labels) to report. If `None` (default), all nodes. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Node ID to its redundancy, between 0 and 1. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a reported node has fewer than two neighbors, or a node does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} For a node with $n$ neighbors, every one of the $n(n - 1)/2$ neighbor pairs is checked for a common neighbor other than the node. Matches NetworkX's `bipartite.node_redundancy`. ## See Also {.doc-see-also} [](`~latapy_clustering`) : Clustering for each node of a bipartite graph. [](`~bipartite_projection`) : Link the nodes of one side through the other. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Ana is the only link between the two clubs, so her redundancy is `0`. Once Ben joins both, each of them could leave without separating the clubs: ::: {#2a5e856b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph.from_edges( [("Ana", "Chess"), ("Ana", "Choir"), ("Ben", "Chess")] ) label = graph.get_label_from_id before = graph.node_redundancy(nodes=["Ana"]) graph.add_edge("Ben", "Choir") after = graph.node_redundancy(nodes=["Ana", "Ben"]) ( {label(n): r for n, r in before.items()}, {label(n): r for n, r in sorted(after.items())}, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ({'Ana': 0.0}, {'Ana': 1.0, 'Ben': 1.0}) ``` ::: ::: ### The only link `davis_southern_women()` links 18 women in a town of the US South in the 1930s to the 14 social events (E1 to E14) each of them attended, and the `bipartite` attribute marks the two sides. Only three women are the sole link between some pair of their events, and Nora Fayette most of all: no other woman attended both E6 and any of E10 to E14: ::: {#220cda16 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} davis = ec.davis_southern_women() women, events = davis.bipartite_sets() redundancy = davis.node_redundancy(nodes=women) [ (davis.get_label_from_id(n), round(r, 3)) for n, r in sorted(redundancy.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1]) if r < 1 ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` [('Nora Fayette', 0.75), ('Helen Lloyd', 0.9), ('Evelyn Jefferson', 0.964)] ``` ::: ::: ::: {#c5ab5504 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} nora_only = ["E6", "E10", "E11", "E12", "E13", "E14"] davis.layout_bipartite(nodes=women, aspect_ratio=0.5).plot( layout="pos", highlight=[("Nora Fayette", e) for e in nora_only], label_by="label", height=900, ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
